cases.title: Pinned ShadowCode is installed, launches in the live session and survives an open/close soak
cases.notes: On ISO 2d8a72e0: case shadowcode PASS (pinned 1.0.0, bundled llama-server/llama-cli report 18f9f7bef, window up 5 min, clean exit, no leftovers). shadowcode-soak 24 cycles: every cycle opened a window and closed cleanly (no SIGKILL, no failed unit), no leftover process, 0 crashes, screen never locked, idle CPU 1.6-6.0% (limit 50%). FAILED only 'available memory after close does not drift down by more than 256 MiB': 680.5 MiB = 87 MiB warm-up + one ~476 MiB step at cycle 4 + 118 MiB noise; the unit's own MemoryCurrent stayed flat (~176-180 MiB) through the step. Diagnostic rerun (sc-diag.tgz): packagekit refresh-cache at ~344 s after the notifier armed its 300 s timer; /var/lib/apt 0.2->207 MB, /var/cache 28->123 MB, Shmem 196->550 MB; ShadowCode home dirs flat after cycle 1. Separately, idle CPU and unit memory peak rise per launch because the window grows ~+52x+99 px per launch on Wayland (tauri-plugin-window-state restores a size including client-side decorations); known issue for 5.0.0 with a maximize workaround, fixed in ShadowCode 1.0.1 (5.0.1). Not proven: a passing memory-drift check on this ISO.

waiver.reason: Release owner chose to ship 5.0.0 on ISO 2d8a72e0 and deliver fixes in 5.0.1 (2026-09-30). The soak failed only its memory-drift check, which a diagnostic rerun attributes to a one-time PackageKit refresh started by the Discover notifier ~300 s after login (~350 MB of apt lists written to the live RAM overlay), not to ShadowCode; and ShadowCode 1.0.0's window grows on each launch under Wayland (window-state plugin restores a CSD-inflated size), fixed in ShadowCode 1.0.1 for 5.0.1.

cases.notes: Focused run on FINAL ISO 2d8a72e0 (installed BIOS clone of ledger install-20260930T193402Z, 4 vCPU/8 GiB, user qa, Plasma Wayland, ShadowCode open), 2026-09-30 22:42-22:48 UTC, host quiet (load 2.2, one VM). Workload: 4 real offline-media missions (60 s 1080p MJPEG clip -> H.264/AAC MP4, decode-verified) queued within 0.5 s on the installed shadowfetch-missions.service worker, one workspace each; all 4 reached waiting-review. Thresholds set before the run (resource_probe.py). ADMISSION: 89 state samples, max 1 mission running, 67 samples with missions queued behind a running one; max 1 concurrent Firebreak sandbox scope; capabilities max_parallel 1; a second worker exited rc0 in 0.15 s without running anything (worker.lock); per-workspace review gate held 3 same-workspace missions queued with 0 running for 368 s while the first awaited review (attempt1). One 0.5 s sample read 2.152 cores vs the 2.10 per-sample threshold: sampler timestamp jitter, lifetime means <= 2.015 and cpu.max unchanged (stated in measurements.log). cases.title: At least 45 minutes concurrent CPU/memory/storage/container/mission/UI stress with clean audits
cases.notes: Two full 2700 s runs on a clone of the 2d8a72e0 BIOS install (user qa), ShadowCode open the whole time. Clean in both: stress-ng rc 0; service classifier 0 faults; no coredumps, kernel faults, OOM kills, thermal events or swap (kernel-oom-faults-thermal.txt is empty, so it is not attached); no failed system/user units; dpkg and btrfs clean; ShadowCode active with its window in all 44 samples and stopped cleanly; CLI latency probe 227/224 cycles, 0 errors, p95 1.05/1.09 s, max 10.5/11.8 s (limit 15 s); min MemAvailable 2277/2324 MiB. Failed in both: mission loop (rc 1) - 'shadowfetch-missions --json show' and 'cancel' returned 'database is busy' at +54 s/+70 s while the worker finalised its first media step (38 s under disk stress), and the stress helper treats busy as fatal; container loop (rc 1) - cycle 3 'podman run --rm' produced the correct checksum but the client did not exit within 120 s, 3 of 22 cycles. The host also carried unrelated load during run 2 (mean 3, peak 7.7 other cores). Not proven: a full mission and container workload loop under 45 min stress on this ISO.

waiver.reason: Release owner chose to ship 5.0.0 on ISO 2d8a72e0 and deliver fixes in 5.0.1 (2026-09-30). Under 45 min of combined CPU/memory/disk stress the system stayed healthy (no crashes, OOM kills, failed units or thermal events; ShadowCode up throughout), but two workload loops stopped early: mission CLI calls hit 'database is busy' after the 10 s lock budget while the worker finalised a step under disk stress, and one 'podman run --rm' client did not exit within 120 s. Root-cause fixes are scheduled for 5.0.1.

Reviewer bundle work/release-5.0.0/evidence-bundle-5.0.0.tar.gz sha256 f7a95161fc787fe9ef3680c9550850b42e174f8860de51e818c8a54f3b13f260 (280 members: acceptance.prepublication.json, approved-inputs.json (92 full-frame PNGs explicitly approved at their digests, all OCR privacy-checked by the visual lanes), every acceptance evidence file, the generated release docs, the detached ISO signature, the named QA source tools, SHA256SUMS, bundle metadata, and qa/5.0.0/evidence-redactions.md). Before packaging, 18 text evidence files had the publisher's home directory replaced with ~ and one harness receipt had the build hostname replaced with <build-host>; nothing else changed; originals are kept privately and evidence-redactions.md lists original and published SHA-256 for each. The extracted bundle (490 files incl. nested archives) was scanned against the local privacy terms and the build hostname: 0 hits. iso.sha256 verifies (sha256sum -c OK) and iso.asc is a Good signature from 8F13CE1535EE1F4A2916A1F73C5C900B7BE80CA1.
